PMID:42668874.setting: Department of Orthopaedics, The Second Hospital of Hebei Medical University (tertiary hospital), Hebei Province; primary unilateral TKA patients
PMID:42668874.standard: not reported (institutional DVT prevention protocol with Caprini assessment; failure modes with RPN > 125 treated as high risk)

cycle1.result: DVT incidence 16/68 (23.53%); length of stay 11.20 ± 4.21 days; 6-week HSS score 76.80 ± 6.90; RPN for the eight high-risk failure modes ranged from 129.79 to 247.88.

PMID:42668874.intervention: Integrated FMEA-RCA programme: multidisciplinary team, workflow mapping, dual nurse-physician Caprini verification, electronic reminders, ISBAR handover checklist, PBL/CBL staff training, HAPA-based patient education with WeChat videos, and head-nurse supervision with twice-weekly spot-check audits.

cycle2.result: DVT incidence 4/68 (5.88%) vs 23.53% (χ2 = 8.442, P = 0.004; aOR 0.24, 95% CI 0.08–0.72, P = 0.011); length of stay 7.99 ± 2.06 days (P < 0.001); 6-week HSS 82.30 ± 5.60 (P < 0.001); all eight RPN values lower (mean relative reduction 36.29%).

PMID:42668874.other_findings: Quasi-experimental before-after comparison of outcomes rather than an audit against a standard; process compliance indicators were monitored but their results are not reported in the text. Largest RPN fall was for poor implementation of postoperative prevention measures (247.88 to 99.73).

PMID:41287689.setting: Orthogeriatric Unit, Northwick Park Hospital, Harrow/London; patients aged 65 and over with acute hip fracture needing surgery
PMID:41287689.standard: BOAST hip fracture standards and NICE guidance on cognitive assessment; AMTS documented at admission, postoperative days 1 and 2, and day 4; target 80% compliance

cycle1.dates: Dates stated inconsistently: July–November 2023 (abstract) or 1 January to 31 March 2024 (methods)
cycle1.result: Initial AMTS 14/30 (46.7%); postoperative day 1 0/30 (0%); postoperative day 2 0/30 (0%); day 4 19/30 (63.3%); overall 33/120 assessments (27.5%).

PMID:41287689.intervention: Automated Cerner EPR alerts prompting AMTS at set timepoints, mandatory 90-minute staff training, AMTS built into handover and ward round templates, visual reminders, and monthly audit feedback.

cycle2.dates: Dates stated inconsistently: November 2023 to January 2024 (abstract) or 1 July to 30 September 2024 (methods)

PMID:41287689.other_findings: Day 4 orthogeriatric AMTS fell and declined month by month in cycle 2 (68% to 41%), suggesting intervention fatigue; no timepoint reached the 80% target. Appropriate responses to abnormal scores rose from 67% to 89%.

PMID:33785283.topic: COVID-19 impact on foot and ankle surgical activity
PMID:33785283.setting: 43 centres across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; adults having foot and ankle surgery in theatre (national multicentre retrospective audit)

cycle1.result: COVID-19 in 35/6644 (0.53%) overall: 0.40% pre-lockdown, 2.11% during lockdown, 0.16% post-lockdown; activity during lockdown 24.44% of pre-lockdown, elective activity 1.73% during and 10.72% after lockdown.

PMID:33785283.other_findings: Infection rates varied by region (highest South East 1.12%, cumulative peak 3.21%); regional anaesthesia use rose significantly during and after lockdown and day-case rates fell.

PMID:37329488.setting: Secondary analysis of the national Physiotherapy Hip Fracture Sprint Audit (England and Wales), linked to HES and PEDW; patients aged 60 and over with surgery for first non-pathological hip fracture
PMID:37329488.standard: Chartered Society of Physiotherapy hip fracture standards cited: minimum total of two hours of physiotherapy in the first postoperative week, physiotherapy assessment and mobilisation within a day of surgery (not used as an audit target in the analysis)

cycle1.dates: Patients operated on in May or June 2017
cycle1.result: ≥2 h physiotherapy in first week: 228 (42.1%) with depression vs 1992 (44.6%) without; physiotherapy on 6–7 days: 91 (16.8%) vs 875 (19.6%). Adjusted OR per 30-min increase for readmission 0.89 (0.81–0.98) vs 0.97 (0.93–1.00), interaction p = 0.09.

PMID:37329488.other_findings: Observational analysis of associations between physiotherapy dose and outcomes by depression diagnosis; no formal interaction reached significance.

PMID:38589258.specialty: Health services research (multiple surgical specialties including orthopaedic trauma)
PMID:38589258.topic: Acceptance of claims-based audit and feedback
PMID:38589258.setting: Online focus groups with medical specialists from 17 academic, top-clinical and general hospitals
PMID:38589258.other_findings: Qualitative study: specialists had mixed views; concerns were validity and reliability of claims data, lack of clinical interpretation and misuse by insurers. Acceptance was higher when feedback comes via professional associations and is not used to judge performance.

PMID:32266437.topic: Fracture liaison service key performance indicators
PMID:32266437.setting: International position paper (IOF Capture the Fracture Working Group, National Osteoporosis Foundation and Fragility Fracture Network)
PMID:32266437.standard: Eleven patient-level FLS KPIs adapted from the UK FLS Database audit; achievement levels red <50%, amber 50–79%, green ≥80% (treatment recommendation target 50%)
PMID:32266437.other_findings: Useful source of audit standards for FLS: e.g. assessment and DXA within 12 weeks, falls assessment, AOM started and follow-up within 16 weeks, AOM persistence at 52 weeks, and data completeness.

PMID:26734180.setting: District general hospital trauma and orthopaedic department (population 320,000, consultant-led 24/7 trauma service)
PMID:26734180.standard: GMC and Royal College of Physicians documentation recommendations: clearly documented PTWR, date/time, consultant on take, clinician leading and documenting, presenting complaint and management plan

cycle1.result: 72% seen on PTWR, 47% of these clearly labelled; 64% of those not seen were weekend admissions; no consultant on take identifiable in 19%, presenting complaint missing in 78%, no plan in 3%, not timed in 17%, no name 19%, no signature 14%, no grade 50%, no contact details 25%.

PMID:26734180.intervention: Trauma Meeting/Post-Take Ward Round proforma on yellow paper, designed with the team (PDSA cycles), results presented at departmental teaching, and weekend surgical juniors briefed to attend the trauma meeting and complete it.

cycle2.dates: Prospective re-audit two weeks after implementation
cycle2.result: Not seen on PTWR fell from 28% to 18% (4% weekend admissions); 88% of those seen had a proforma; 18% of all cases had no proforma; consultant unidentifiable in 4%; all entries signed and dated; no name 12%, no contact details 15%, no grade 10%.

PMID:26734180.other_findings: Weekend proforma completion stayed poor (67% of cases without a proforma were weekend admissions); all remaining documentation gaps were in cases without a proforma.

PMID:31521618.setting: Carle Hospital, Urbana, Illinois; hospitalised hip fracture patients (prospective QI project with medical record audit)
PMID:31521618.standard: Evidence-based delirium prevention protocol; records audited with the CHART-DEL instrument
PMID:31521618.intervention: Evidence-based hip fracture delirium prevention protocol introduced.

cycle2.result: Delirium incidence 15.6% (not statistically significant); protocol used by admitting physicians in 31% of admissions; prevention interventions documented by nurses in 75.6% of records.

PMID:31521618.other_findings: Abstract only; low physician uptake of the protocol (31%).
